text:
Maya (Support): Heads-up: acme-prod seeing ~50% 503s for the authenticated /v1/toolcall endpoint over the last 7m. Spike started at ~17:10 UTC. Gateway logs show 'upstream inference worker exited unexpectedly'. Customer on the line now. :rotating_light:

Tom (oncall): Investigating. Can you paste root logs and a sample request id? Any JWT/auth errors? @Priya fyi.

Maya (Support): Sample req id: req_02f9a1c3. Pasting clipped logs from the runner: ```ERROR runtime: segfault at 0xdeadbeef
GPU memory exceeded: attempted 24.3GB > 24.0GB
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Backtrace (most recent call last): ...``` Also see container restart events ~every 30s for that pool.

Priya (eng-runtime): Looking at infra metrics — GPU mem spike on pool "dedicated-hosted-1" exactly correlates with the 503 ramp. OOM counter increments then kube restarts the pod. Workload is heavy toolcall with large context + multimodal attachments (customer-supplied). Seems the runtime tried to allocate a KV cache + model cache and exceeded device mem.

Nora (eng-sre): Can we temporarily throttle the priority queue and route heavy toolcalls to a lower-concurrency variant? Immediate mitigations: set routing policy to cap concurrency to 1 per-connection for that customer, and force fallback to quantized variant for requests with context > 8k tokens. Also consider rolling back the recent canary to rule out regression.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-18T17:05Z - canary rollout: model-serve v2.14.7 -> pool dedicated-hosted-1 (instances: 3 -> 6).

Tom (oncall): OK — start rollback of v2.14.7 on dedicated-hosted-1 now. @Priya can you enable core/heap collection and preserve nvcrash artifacts? Add RUNNER_DEBUG=1 to the pod and `--preserve-crash=true`. Also grab `kubectl top pod <pod>` and `dmesg` from node.

Priya (eng-runtime): Started capture. Repro steps customer provided (short): ```for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '@heavy_toolcall.json' https://api.redwood.com/v1/toolcall ; done``` They use short-lived signed JWTs (30s TTL) and send bursts of concurrent requests. Noted retries piling up when tokens refresh mid-burst.

Sam (CS): Customer is seeing a billing spike because of automatic retries. CS asked if we can credit/remove retry charges while we investigate. Customer on call waiting for mitigation.

Maya (Support): Action plan we told customer: 1) rollback canary on impacted pool (in progress), 2) throttle priority toolcall route to 5 qps for that org, 3) collect core + nvcrash + kube events and share repro req ids. I'll update them in 15m.

Tom (oncall): Acknowledged. If OOM continues after rollback, next step: pin to quantized-8bit variant on that pool and enable aggressive kv-cache eviction (`KV_MAX_BYTES=128M`). We'll also look at batching/burst throttles.

Nora (eng-sre): Addendum — enable `--dump-kv=true` for the next 10 minutes on the repro pod so we can verify the cache growth pattern. If you hit a repro, DM me the req id and I will pull the heap snapshot. :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): Will follow up with collected artifacts and timeline. Current state: rollback started, throttles applied, core capture running. Escalating to eng for forensic analysis.
